Rules summary You have two options on your turn: "Produce" or Take a "Supporting Action" followd by a "Main Action" Contents 1 Produce Turn 2 Action Turn 2.1 Supporting Actions 2.2 Main Actions 2.3 Free Actions 3 Dice Faces 4 Extra bonuses 5 Victory Points 6 Game End Produce Turn When you produce, the following happens: Keep up to 3 resource dice, discard the rest (wild tokens are not dice). Discard any number of cards from your hand. If you have less than 5 cards, draw until you have 5. Roll and add all the resource dice (brown boxes on your corporation card + green project cards). Ready blue project cards (yellow, green and red arrows). Action Turn You take one supporting action, and one main action. (As a main action you can do a second supporting action) Supporting Actions Roll and add 1 die of any color. Pay 1 resource die (any): to turn another die any side. Pay 1 resource die (any): to draw 2 cards. Use a ready yellow arrow action (blue cards) (this card will be unavailable until you take a produce turn). Main Actions Perform a second support action. Play a card from hand (paying its cost in matching resource dice). Pay 3 heat resources: to increase temperature 1 step. Pay 3 water resources: to place 1 ocean tile. Pay 4 plant resources: to place 1 forest tile (and increase oxygen 1 step). Pay 3 city resources: to place 1 city tile. Pay 3 MegaCredit: resources to immediately gain 2 VP. Use a red arrow action (blue cards) (this card will be unavailable until you take a produce turn). Free Actions Use green arrow action (this card will be unavailable until you take a produce turn). Free actions that can be used at any time. Dice Faces Some resources are harder to get. Common have 3 faces (50%), uncommon 2 faces (33%), rare 1 face (16%). Yellow Green Blue Gray Red Common (3x) Megacredit Plant Energy Steel Heat Uncommon (2x) Science Microbe Water Titanium Event Rare (1x) Earth Animal Oxygen City Nuclear Extra bonuses on terraformation tracks (oxygen and temperature) sometimes you get bonus resource dice when placing a forest, city etc get covered bonuses when reacing 5 and 12 green VP (tracked during the game, not at the end) gain and play a special bonus card frome the bonus pool (2 cards per player) Victory Points Ocean - Gain 2 VP (because it counts as terraforming). Forest - Gain 1 VP per adjacent city when placing tile. (If Oxygen is increased 1 step, Gain 2 VP for terraforming.) City - Gain 2VP plus 1 VP per adjacent forest. Heat - Gain 2 VP (because it counts as terraforming). Oxygen - Gain 2 VP (because it counts as terraforming). Green Ribbon - Score the printed VPs immediately . Red Ribbon - Score these VPs at the end of the game . Game End When two out of three of the following "Terraforming" conditions are met, the end of the game is triggered. All players get one last turn (including the player who just completed the second parameter). The oxygen track is completed. The temperature track is completed. All ocean tiles have been placed. Players add victory points from Red Ribbons: Cards Milestones (4VP, first player to complete) Awards (5 VP first place, 3 VP second place; most of a die symbol in cards cost; in 2 player game no 2nd place) Tiebreaker (dice production).

---

Terraforming Mars: The Dice Game is a card-driven dice game in which players use special dice to develop their corporations and terraform Mars into a new home for humanity. The dice represent resources that players spend to play cards and perform other actions. During the game, you increase your production of dice, terraform, place cities and greenery tiles on the board, and gain various bonuses. Each turn, you either produce new dice (Production Turn) or perform actions (Action Turn).

Whenever you terraform Mars (raise oxygen or temperature, or place an ocean tile), you gain 2 Victory Points (VP). You can also gain VP for placing tiles and playing cards, as well as winning Awards and Milestones.

The game ends when two of the three global parameters — oxygen/temperature/ocean — have been completed. The player with most VP wins.
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] What's worse than a cheesy reduced card game version of a game? A dice game version!  This is pure cash grab!  While this looks a lot better than "Ares Expedition" (looks+mechanics), it still rubs me the wrong way to an extent that I want to scream.  The game uses its own exotic card format. That is a really bad and despicable practice!  Also, the game is super random (because centered around dice) and not thematic. You can easily get stuck with cards that you can't play because you don't roll the right resources.   [quote]Do you need to have played the original TFM to play or enjoy this?[/quo

[Rating: 1/10] Really pissed at the ridiculous shipping cost. Will put it up to a reasonable rating if the game doesn't suck. (The card game was a real disappointment.)

[Rating: 1/10] I wasn't enamoured with this dice game format. It seems that I want the thrill of dice rolling when playing "the Dice Game" versions of these. And this game doesn't offer that.  This could have been an opportunity to offer a different vibe to Terraforming Mars's rather calculating Cube Accountancy. Instead, it's really just TFM but with dice rolling. In which case, why aren't you playing the board game instead?

[Rating: 1/10] TERRAFORMING MARS pared down and bungled by (more) randomization in the form of resource dice. But, having said that, and considering my general distaste for TFM, I would almost certainly play this over the original if given the explicit choice between the two. Less downtime, less of a slog, less of a trudge, all that jazz.  [b]Update:[/b] What I said above is still true. I [i]would[/i] play this over the original TFM. That does not, however, make this a good game.

[Rating: 1/10] "Terraforming Mars: the luck game" - luck in dice, luck in cards, and an end-game scoring that is a close game no matter what you do. Feels like playing the card game War where there's no rhyme or reason to anything that happens. Maybe that is fine for a short game, but this was not short.  This game should not exist - a waste of everyone's time.

[Rating: 2/10] We were duped in to thinking we were getting 2 neoprene mats for the game. Flat out lied and made them double sided and have the nerve to keep it posted that we are getting 2 mats.

[Rating: 2/10] A complete joke/tragedy of a game with randomness upon randomness - and of course fuck all but “homepathic interaction”. Moronic order of production steps which maximize the randomness instead reducing it. Moronic lack of an action to re-roll dice - you need to spend a whole turn to change a single die. Moronic lack of mechanism to exchange “common” ~ “uncommon” ~ “rare” dice rolls.
